explanation:
[EFFECT]
The hour of the day has a strongly non-monotonic, bimodal effect on predicted demand. Demand is heavily suppressed in the early morning hours, reaching its lowest point around 4 a.m. (contribution ≈ −2.81), then rises sharply through the morning commute, peaking at 8 a.m. (contribution ≈ +1.11). After a mild midday plateau of moderate positive contributions (roughly 10 a.m.–4 p.m.), demand surges again to the overall daily peak at 5 p.m. (contribution ≈ +1.22), before declining steadily through the evening and back into negative territory by midnight.

[IMPORTANCE]
Hour of day is the single most influential feature in the model, ranking 1st out of all 9 features with an importance score of 0.89. It has a far larger impact on predicted rentals than any other variable.

[RECOMMENDATION]
Bike availability and staffing should be concentrated around the two daily peaks — the morning commute (around 8 a.m.) and the evening commute (around 5–6 p.m.) — as these hours drive demand far above the daily average, while overnight hours (roughly 1–5 a.m.) consistently see very low rentals and require minimal resources.
